intro: Beside the Selimiye Mosque, in Edirne province, stands the Edirne Museum, opened in 1971. Under one roof it brings together the finds of the Thracian dolmens and tumuli and the ethnography of Edirne, once the Ottoman capital.
history: The museum beside the Selimiye Mosque opened in 1971. It holds together two very different worlds: the finds of the Thracian dolmens and tumuli, which reach back to the second millennium BC, and the ethnography of a city that was the Ottomans' second capital.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the finds from the Thracian dolmens and the Roman and Byzantine works, then the Edirnekâri lacquerwork, and finally the Kırkpınar section.
facts: Did you know? The Edirnekâri work shown here is a technique of painting and lacquering on wood that developed in this city alone. And the dolmens of Thrace, reaching back to the second millennium BC, represent a burial tradition with no parallel elsewhere in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our journey through the Edirne Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. From ancient Thrace to Ottoman Edirne, these pieces are in your care for a moment; let them pass on unharmed. Enjoy your visit.
